t: Chapter 16 · A Stroll Round the Capital
b: the bus had started going in the opposite direction from where I had to get off .. And there was no one else on the bus .. From Kathirgama Kandan on, there was no god I didn't pray to.. Afraid of which forest he'd drop me in, I went to talk to the driver and he didn't even turn round… Well, that's the full stop to the Vietnam story, I thought, and he braked…..

Straight away I phoned our lot and asked where they were.. When they sent the location saying it was close, though he told me not to, I grabbed everything and got off.. If he dropped me in some forest no one's ever seen, who'd come looking
I arrived at dawn on Saturday.. It had been a week since we set out… Like an old porter carrying sacks, I came with my bundles on my head and somehow found the others
Hanoi… it looked like a concrete graveyard…Not very pretty at all… We got a car at once and went to the room.. He'd put us on the fifth floor.. Going up and down alone took half my life

When we went out in the morning, right downstairs there were lots of shops… When we looked for things to buy for our people, terribly expensive… That's when she gave us the wonderful information that we should have bought everything in Hoi An itself… She'd cleverly bought everything there… Well, who cares if the money goes, we can't buy it later, we said, and bought a few things

After that they dragged me off saying we had to see the train.. As if she's going to show me a train I haven't seen in Wellawatte… When I asked, apparently the train comes through a lane… people stand right beside it on both sides and watch, she said..The reason I cut down going to the Wellawatte sea is so I don't get hit going close to that train…And Varnam Sir taught us that by Bernoulli's principle, if you stand close to a moving train the pressure difference will push you onto it… Since then I don't get on a train until it stops

But how do I make her understand by saying this … the other three coming along are physics tigers.. Fine, we went, and we were late .. They'd closed the barrier and the police akka wouldn't let us in… Look at this: just as they were closing, I popped in like a cashew nut sticking out.. That police akka hit me on the back and pushed me out… Luckily only our lot saw… Laughing (and a little hurt too).. we watched from outside for the train to come

Getting cheeky over this, Mithra stood on tiptoe on the gate to look.. She really is a bit short, so as she couldn't see she leaned over, and a man threw a soda cap and scolded her to get down… He aimed it perfectly.. You could send him to a shooting competition … With all this drama, having seen that stately Thiruvarur chariot, we set off for the next place..
note: Hanoi's "train street", where trains pass within inches of houses and cafés, is a famous sight. The Thiruvarur temple chariot in Tamil Nadu is one of the largest in India; the author jokingly gives the train the same grandeur. "Akka" means elder sister, a polite way to address a woman.
